I farm only 4.1 mu, so every bag of fertilizer matters, but I still do not like cutting too hard on inputs because if yield drops, that loss hurts more than wasting a little fertilizer. For wheat, I will mostly follow what has worked in our area for years: improved wheat seed, rotary tillage after maize, enough base fertilizer, then one good spring topdressing with water from the well. Our side in Quzhou usually depends on water at the key stages, so I will give wheat about 3 irrigations if the season is normal: once at turning green, once around jointing, and once at grain filling if the ground is dry. After wheat harvest, I will rush into summer maize because the stubble season is tight. I will use hybrid maize seed because around here the hybrids usually stand better and yield better than old seed. I will keep tillage simple with rotary work after wheat, put most phosphorus and potassium in early, split nitrogen so the maize does not go hungry at jointing, and give about 2 irrigations if rain is not enough. On such a small farm, I can manage the field myself with family help, so I will keep a close eye on weeds, armyworm, aphids, rust, and ear diseases, and I will spray when needed, usually 2 times for wheat and 2 times for maize in a normal year. This plan is not fancy; it is the kind of steady plan I trust because it matches local practice, fits my money, and protects yield.
